protocol.py: 4 biology problems (1 error, 2 warnings, 1 note).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: water (tube C3 in slot 3)
   line 52:  p20.aspirate(12, tube_rack["C3"])
   At line 52 the tip went into water (tube C3 in slot 3) while it still carried plasmid 1
   (tube A1 in slot 3), plasmid 2 (tube A2 in slot 3), plasmid 3 (tube A3 in slot 3),
   plasmid 4 (tube A4 in slot 3) and 10 more from an earlier step (this line did it 12
   times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from
   it then took the unwanted material along into 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6,
   A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 2.
   Affected: tube C3 in slot 3.
   Also reached 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 52 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [4cd3f9a14d5b]

2. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: enzyme
   line 46:  p20.dispense(1, dest_well)
   At line 46 the robot put enzyme into wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in
   slot 2 (this line did it 12 times). Take well A1 in slot 2: at that moment it held only 2
   ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 53, to make the 14 ul
   of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is
   meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought
   the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many
   times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star
   activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 2:
   water and buffer first, then the sample, then enzyme last. Or make a master mix of water,
   buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html
   Source: Promega: restriction enzyme resource (add the enzyme last; glycerol and star
   activity)
           https://www.promega.com/resources/guides/nucleic-acid-analysis/restriction-enzyme-resource/
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   Source: Qiagen: critical factors for successful real-time PCR (order of addition)
           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf
   [f35af3c11ea6]

3. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 12 stocks
   line 49:  p20.aspirate(5, tube_rack[plasmid_well])
   At line 49 the tip went into plasmid 1 (tube A1 in slot 3), plasmid 2 (tube A2 in slot
   3), plasmid 3 (tube A3 in slot 3), plasmid 4 (tube A4 in slot 3) and 8 more while it
   still carried buffer (tube C1 in slot 3) and enzyme (tube C2 in slot 3) from an earlier
   step (this line did it 12 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it
   in the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong
   there. The protocol does not draw from them again, so this run is not harmed, but what is
   left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: tubes A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 4 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 49 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [a6a3112bb89e]

4. NOTE CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: enzyme (tube C2 in slot 3)
   line 45:  p20.aspirate(1, tube_rack["C2"])
   At line 45 the tip went into enzyme (tube C2 in slot 3) while it still carried buffer
   (tube C1 in slot 3) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a
   little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does
   not belong there. The protocol drew from it again afterwards, but only into wells that
   were given that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in
   the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: tube C2 in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 45 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [075aa476cbdc]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
